takeaways.cover: They have to be here for the talent. They want to be in the office. Tour the vacant LS product that already has power.
takeaways.thesis: 150 Industrial is the tour: 230,961 SF, former Novartis, robotics user, six groups in process.
takeaways.leasing: Demand died after the COVID build. The leftover shells are the AI inventory — if the MEP is real.
takeaways.office: Peninsula office is 23.8% vacant. That is not the AI product. Talent still comes to the office.
takeaways.product: High-powered AI tenant: 30 W/SF min, prefer 35–50+. Excess transformer and 40% backup.
takeaways.talent: Bay Area is #1. 57% of listings are AI. Remote is 7%. They will sit in the building.
takeaways.funding: 80% of U.S. AI VC since 2020 lands here. LS funding is the residual.
takeaways.mission-bay: Highest SF asking $7.37/sf FSG vs city $5.73/sf FSG. Tour 1450 Owens. Overflow is Potrero / Dogpatch / Peninsula.
takeaways.compression: Do not put type on the city. Overflow from the compressed waterfront is Potrero / Dogpatch / Peninsula. 8.1 msf, 36% AI.
takeaways.inventory: Tour the vacant new-construction LS shells and 1450 Owens. 150 Industrial is a closed deal. Mission Rock B is not 100% vacant.
takeaways.power: 30 W/SF minimum, prefer 35–50+. Avia/Spur lab is 8 W/USF. May 2026 working file is a different vintage.
takeaways.decision: What do you tour this quarter — and does it already have the MEP?

takeaways.cover: Vacant high-infrastructure R&D is the conversion bid. Commodity office is not.
takeaways.thesis: A CGT/GLP-1 shell became a robotics building because the utilities were already there.
takeaways.leasing: 30.2% Bay Area science vacant. The paper that printed is still purpose-built. The empty shells are the AI tour.
takeaways.office: 23.8% Peninsula vacancy does not become an AI bid without power and MEP.
takeaways.product: Hold or convert only if 30 W/SF and transformer excess exist. That is the sale against vacant LS shells.
takeaways.talent: AI companies require in-person. 30% of SF office activity since 2023 is AI-related.
takeaways.funding: Office investment $9.091B is not lease-up. 80% of AI VC is the demand signal.
takeaways.mission-bay: Highest asking in the city. LS 51.9% vacant. 1450 Owens is the vacant cold shell. NVIDIA is chatter.
takeaways.compression: The waterfront is compressed. Conversion inventory is the vacant LS shell, not more office on the city fabric.
takeaways.inventory: Vacant new-construction shells are the overbuild. 1450 Owens is the Mission Bay tour. Do not list 150 Industrial or Mission Rock B as vacant.
takeaways.power: 30 W/SF min is the Feb 3 sale against vacant LS shells. Do not underwrite May power as February market.
takeaways.decision: Hold, convert, or sell into the user who already printed at 150 Industrial.

takeaways.cover: Credit follows in-office AI and power delivery — not vacancy averages.
takeaways.thesis: Six high-credit groups in process on one 230,961 SF box. That is residual-risk information.
takeaways.leasing: 16-year UCSF paper and a vacant CGT shell are not the same credit.
takeaways.office: Peninsula office gave back 93k SF. In-office AI is not a takeout for every empty floor.
takeaways.product: Underwrite 30 W/SF min and 40% backup. If it is not there, it is not an AI loan.
takeaways.talent: 375,730 tech workers. NY Metro is larger on headcount. The Bay Area is still #1 on the scorecard — and 80% of AI VC.
takeaways.funding: $47.42B Q4 venture. LS $2.7B is residual. Debt thaw is not occupancy.
takeaways.mission-bay: Highest asking $7.37/sf FSG vs city $5.73/sf FSG. +154,895 in the quarter / +180k YTD. NVIDIA is chatter, not a closed-comp print.
takeaways.compression: 8.1 msf already in. 36% AI. Do not underwrite overflow as if Mission Bay still has empty waterfront office.
takeaways.inventory: 1450 Owens is 215k vacant at $7.75/sf NNN. 150 Industrial is leased robotics. Mission Rock B has Coinbase signed. NVIDIA is chatter.
takeaways.power: Underwrite 30 W/SF min and 40% backup. May power vintage is older — do not lend as if it is the February snapshot.
takeaways.decision: Where do you put debt this quarter — and on whose delivery clock?
